title: Will India’s Growth Keep Defying Global Headwinds?
gist: Renewed US-Iran fighting has pushed Brent to US$95/bbl and driven US and European bond yields to multi-year highs (a multi-decade high in Japan), reviving stagflation fears. Against that backdrop India printed 7.8% YoY GDP growth for the June quarter; Gavekal argues opposition accusations of statistical manipulation are exaggerated and the economy is genuinely sound, with sustained high oil the main threat.

insights.claim: Renewed fighting between the United States and Iran has pushed Brent crude to US$95/bbl, lifting inflation expectations and threatening global consumption and growth.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A geopolitically-driven oil spike to US$95 is the live input to the stagflation trade: watch energy longs versus consumer-discretionary and rate-sensitive shorts.
insights.quote: The resumption in fighting between the United States and Iran has pushed Brent to US$95/bbl, raising inflation expectations and threatening consumption and growth.
insights.locator: Once again, the specter of stagflation

insights.claim: Bond yields in the US and Europe are at multi-year highs and Japanese yields at a multi-decade high as markets price in monetary tightening.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Japan's multi-decade yield high is the outlier worth watching, since it pressures the global carry complex and repatriation flows.
insights.quote: Bond yields in the US and Europe are hitting multi-year highs—and a multi-decade high in Japan—as markets price in monetary tightening
insights.locator: Bond yields in the US and Europe

insights.claim: Rising bond yields are raising borrowing costs on debt loads described as already eye-watering, compounding the stagflation squeeze on sovereigns.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Debt-service math, not inflation alone, is the transmission channel to watch for fiscal stress and curve steepening.
insights.quote: jacking up borrowing costs on already eye-watering debt loads
insights.locator: as markets price in monetary tightening

themes.theme: India as the outlier bright spot

insights.claim: India's headline GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the quarter ended June 2026, faster than expected.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A 7.8% print with oil at US$95 makes India the clearest growth carve-out from the global stagflation narrative.
insights.quote: headline GDP growth of 7.8% YoY in the quarter ended June
insights.locator: Modi this week described headline GDP growth

insights.claim: India's faster-than-expected growth is the single bright spot within an otherwise gloomy global macro picture of oil shocks and surging yields.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Argues for relative-value overweight of Indian equities and growth assets against developed-market rate-sensitive exposure.
insights.quote: But within the gloom there is a shaft of light: faster-than-expected growth in India.

insights.claim: India delivered its growth acceleration in the face of oil-price shocks and supply-chain disruptions, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi characterized as a Herculean feat.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Political framing matters for policy continuity: a government claiming credit for growth is less likely to pivot to demand-suppressing austerity.
insights.quote: “Doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed… yet again!”
insights.locator: Modi this week described headline GDP growth

insights.claim: Sustained higher oil prices are flagged as the main risk that could dampen India's growth run, despite the strong June-quarter print.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat Brent staying near US$95 as the key trigger for downgrading the Indian growth and current-account outlook.
insights.quote: India’s economy is in good shape, even if sustained higher oil prices risk dampening Modi’s mood.

insights.claim: A senior Indian opposition leader dismissed the GDP figures as statistical gymnastics, alleging the government used methodological revisions to mask a bleak economic reality.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Data-credibility attacks are the standing bear case on India; know the argument before it resurfaces around the next print.
insights.quote: accusing the government of using methodological revisions to fix the data while “hiding India’s bleak economic reality.”

insights.claim: Gavekal judges accusations that India manipulates its GDP data to be exaggerated if not entirely misplaced, and holds that the underlying economy is genuinely in good shape.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Taking the 7.8% print at face value removes the main discount investors apply to Indian macro data and supports staying long the growth story.
